words.definition: a piece of furniture with a door and shelves for keeping things
words.example: The plates and cups are in the kitchen {cupboard}.

words.definition: a flat board on a wall where you put things
words.example: The top {shelf} of the bookcase is full.

words.definition: pieces of cloth that cover a window
words.example: Close the {curtains} when it gets dark.

words.definition: a soft thing where you put your head in bed
words.example: There is a feather {pillow} under my head.

words.definition: a warm cover for a bed
words.example: It's cold tonight, so take another {blanket}.

words.definition: what you say or write when someone asks you something
words.example: I know the {answer} to that question!

words.definition: something that is wrong
words.example: I made a {mistake}, so I used my rubber.

words.definition: an important test at school
words.example: I studied hard for my maths {exam}.

words.definition: a book that tells you what words mean
words.example: Look up the new word in the {dictionary}.

words.definition: a list that shows when lessons or trains happen
words.example: Our {timetable} says we have art after lunch.

words.definition: something you learn at school, like maths or art
words.example: My favourite {subject} at school is science.

words.definition: the study of what happened in the past
words.example: In {history}, we learn about kings and queens.

words.definition: the study of countries, mountains, rivers and seas
words.example: In {geography}, we learn where countries are on a map.

words.definition: a list of what you need and the steps to cook a dish
words.example: Grandma's {recipe} for apple pie is the best.

words.definition: tasting very good
words.example: This chocolate cake is {delicious}!

words.definition: food that you eat at one time, like breakfast or dinner
words.example: Dinner is my favourite {meal} of the day.

words.definition: a list of the food you can choose in a restaurant
words.example: The waiter gave us the {menu} to choose our food.

words.definition: a plant, like a carrot or a potato, that you eat
words.example: Broccoli is my favourite green {vegetable}.

words.definition: very happy because something good will happen soon
words.example: I can't wait for my party; I'm so {excited}!

words.definition: feeling that something you did not expect has happened
words.example: I didn't expect a party, so I was {surprised}.

words.definition: thinking that something bad might happen
words.example: I am {worried} that I will fail the test.

words.definition: pleased about something good that you or someone close to you did
words.example: My parents are {proud} of me because I worked hard.

words.definition: sad because you are alone
words.example: With no friends to play with, I felt {lonely}.

words.definition: quiet and not worried or excited
words.example: Take a deep breath and stay {calm}.

words.definition: not able to understand something
words.example: I'm {confused}: is it Monday or Tuesday today?

words.definition: a group of people who play a sport together
words.example: There are eleven players in a football {team}.

words.definition: a person who takes part in a sport or game
words.example: She is the best {player} in our team.

words.definition: when people run, swim or drive to see who is fastest
words.example: Tom came first in the running {race}.

words.definition: to be the best in a game or competition
words.example: If we score more goals, we will {win} the match.

words.definition: to not win a game
words.example: If we {lose} this match, we are out.

words.definition: to get a goal or a point in a game
words.example: He kicked the ball hard to {score} a goal.

words.definition: to do something again and again to get better at it
words.example: I {practise} the piano every day.

words.definition: the long part at the back of an animal's body
words.example: The happy dog is wagging its {tail}.

words.definition: a very small animal with six legs
words.example: An ant is a kind of {insect}.

words.definition: a person who brings food to your table in a restaurant
words.example: The restaurant {waiter} brought our food to the table.

words.definition: a person whose job is to clean buildings
words.example: The {cleaner} keeps our school floors clean and tidy.

words.definition: a person who helps people in a shop
words.example: The {shop assistant} helped me find my size.

words.definition: a person who designs machines, roads or bridges
words.example: An {engineer} designs bridges, roads and machines.

words.definition: a person who makes bread and cakes to sell
words.example: The {baker} gets up early to make bread.

words.definition: a place by the road where you wait for a bus
words.example: We waited at the {bus stop} for the number 9.

words.definition: a place where people buy petrol for their cars
words.example: We need petrol, so let's stop at the {petrol station}.

words.definition: the path at the side of a road where people walk
words.example: People walk on the {pavement} beside the road.

words.definition: a place where people leave their cars
words.example: There are no free spaces in the {car park}.

words.definition: a place where roads meet and cars drive around in a circle
words.example: Drive around the {roundabout} and take the second exit.

words.definition: something built over a river so you can cross it
words.example: We walked across the {bridge} over the river.

words.definition: a wide road where cars can go very fast between cities
words.example: The {motorway} is a big, fast road between cities.

words.definition: the flat part of a TV or computer where you see pictures
words.example: Don't sit too close to the TV {screen}.

words.definition: words that you send or leave for someone
words.example: I got a text {message} from my mum.

words.definition: a secret word that lets you use a computer
words.example: My {password} is a secret word that opens my computer.

words.definition: the area outside the Earth, where the stars and planets are
words.example: Astronauts travel into {space} in a rocket.

words.definition: a hard material you can see through, used for windows
words.example: Be careful! The window is made of {glass}.

words.definition: a hard, shiny material used to make cars and coins
words.example: Coins and keys are made of {metal}.

words.definition: a yellow metal that costs a lot of money
words.example: Coins made of {gold} are yellow and very expensive.

words.definition: a soft material from a plant, used to make clothes
words.example: This soft {cotton} comes from a plant.

words.definition: things that you throw away because you do not want them
words.example: Old food and empty boxes are all {rubbish}.

words.definition: a light material used to make bottles and bags
words.example: We should use less {plastic} to keep the sea clean.

words.definition: dirty air, water or land that harms living things
words.example: Cars and factories cause air {pollution}.

words.definition: to keep someone or something safe
words.example: We must {protect} wild animals and their homes.

words.definition: plants, animals and everything in the world that people did not make
words.example: We went for a {nature} walk in the forest.

words.definition: the power that makes machines work, like electricity
words.example: We save {energy} when we turn off the lights.

words.definition: to keep something in your mind
words.example: Can you {remember} the name of our first teacher?

words.definition: to not remember something
words.example: Don't {forget} to brush your teeth!

words.definition: to choose what to do after thinking
words.example: I can't choose, so you {decide}.

words.definition: to tell someone about something so they understand it
words.example: Can you {explain} this word? I don't understand it.

words.definition: to take something that you will give back later
words.example: Can I {borrow} your pencil, please?

words.definition: to give something to someone for a short time
words.example: I can {lend} you my bike until Friday.

words.definition: to get to a place
words.example: When we {arrive} home, we will have dinner.

words.definition: to go away from a place
words.example: We must {leave} now; goodbye, everyone!

words.definition: to ask someone to come to a party
words.example: I want to {invite} all my friends to my party.

words.definition: every time
words.example: The sun {always} rises in the east.

words.definition: most of the time
words.example: I {usually} walk, but today I took the bus.

words.definition: not at any time
words.example: Penguins {never} fly.

words.definition: fast
words.example: Hurry up! Eat {quickly} or we will miss the bus.

words.definition: not fast; taking a long time
words.example: The tortoise is not fast; it moves very {slowly}.

words.definition: making very little noise
words.example: Speak {quietly} in the library, please.

words.definition: thinking about what you do so nothing goes wrong
words.example: Hold the baby {carefully}; don't drop her!

words.definition: making a lot of noise
words.example: The dog barked {loudly} and woke everyone up.
